deviations.description: Rule A is effectively ignored: when the coverage goal exceeds the hot-spot cap (cov > cap) and no other rule applies, the network sends the request to automated planning instead of escalating. This was seen for gaps from 1 Gy to 24 Gy across the input ranges. Only a few such requests escalated, and only when other inputs were already near another rule's threshold (e.g. cord floor about 1 Gy below the cord goal).
deviations.condition: (cov > cap + 0.3) and (missing == 0) and not ((mand_in_ptv - 0.05*ptv_vol > 0.1) and (cov > mand_lim)) and (cord_lim >= cord_floor)

deviations.description: Rule D fails in part of the input space: with missing = 1, requests with low cov, high cap, high mand_lim, high cord_lim, low cord_floor and a large PTV are sent to planning, because the other inputs outweigh the missing-structure term. The condition is a boundary fitted from local slopes around these points; it is approximate away from the tested area.
